newsitem.title: UK: Royal Bank defends Scottish banknote issue.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank defends Scottish banknote issue.

text.p: Royal Bank of Scotland, one of three Scottish banks that issues banknotes independently, said on Thursday the system should continue even if Britain decides to enter the EMU at some date.

Royal Bank said it is working with other Scottish note issuers, Bank of Scotland and Clydesdale Bank, part of National Australia Bank, to ensure the survival of Scottish notes which, uniquely in Britain, still include a one pound denomination.
"Our initial view is that we see no reason why the practice which has lasted for 270 years should not continue," Royal Bank chairman Lord Younger of Prestwick told its annual meeting.
Younger said the bank has been in discussions with the Bank of England and the European Monetary Institute on the subject.
He said he was confident that agreement could be reached which, adding that it was Royal Bank's view that Britain was unlikely to enter EMU in the first wave in 1999.
Younger said Royal bank was busy making preparations for the new Euro currency especially given the implications for its treasury business and the needs of its large corporate customers.
